items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I admire him tremendously and we are very good friends.

ctx.x: We've talked a little bit about Freddy Jenkins, but really not too much. I know he was with the Collegians and then later, of course, he was with Ellington.

Yes, Freddy was with me in Wilberforce, and he was quite a showman. He always carried that label, even into Duke Ellington's band. He could play, and he was a good reader. He was a good reader. And he never complained about a sore lip. That's one thing, you know. Trumpet players, a lot of them have trouble with their lips. He never had a sore lip. The only thing that -- you know, just to get on him about -- I think I mentioned it before -- he played more or less -- to an empty house he played better than he did…

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: We had a couple of cars... I had a little guy with me... He was one of my trumpet players. I guess you've heard the name Freddie Jenkins.

ctx.x: I believe I have, you bet.

Well, he was at Wilberforce, and the funny thing about it -- we didn't have any uniforms or anything - not many clothes at that time. We were struggling. But Wilberforce University had a fire at one time, and everybody loved Freddie Jenkins so much after the fire; he had a wardrobe that was more extensive than any six guys, you know. And we kidded him about it. But He could play. He was always a salesman. But there was only one thing that I regretted about him -- he would do -- invariably do. We would go and play…
What year were you in school, like freshman, sophomore, or whatever, when you began this?
